hero.headline: Hobe Sound gets first Aldi grocery store opening July 9 at former Winn-Dixie site
hero.teaser: Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi store, opening Wednesday at 8867 SE Bridge Road in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be.
hero.body:
The new grocery store is opening July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road, in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be. Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years. There will be a grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 9 at 8:30 a.m., and the first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card.

The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce commissioners reject Little Jim Bait & Tackle lawsuit settlement over waterfront permit violations
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer in a lawsuit alleging years of waterfront mismanagement tied to histo.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer in a lawsuit alleging years of waterfront mismanagement tied to historic restaurant Little Jim Bait & Tackle. Plaintiff Kevin Keene said he will continue to pursue litigation against the city following the vote. The city has filed a motion to dismiss Keene's amended complaint. Under the proposed settlement terms, Keene would have dropped the case if the city halted any new plans for Little Jim until Florida Department of Environmental Protection permit issues are resolved and allowed a public vote on future waterfront land decisions. Documents WPTV obtained from the FDEP claim the city has been operating docks on state-owned submerged land at Little Jim without the required permits since 2021. The state agency has ordered the city to pay nearly $16,000 by July 17.

City Commissioner Michael Broderick acknowledged the permit issue is true and said someone at some point extended the docks further than allowed. Broderick plans to negotiate FDEP's fines down while the city investigates who authorized the extension. The dispute traces back to last year when the Fort Pierce landmark of nearly 80 years faced an uncertain future after its lease expired. The city offered up the land lease for bidders, much to the outcry of residents. After an outpouring of community support, the city kept the restaurant open month to month. Despite five formal proposals submitted to the city, including one from the current operators, the city said none met the criteria and scrapped plans to pick a new tenant. Keene argues the Little Jim process was marked by instability, changing information and unresolved material issues, and that Little Jim's is part of a broader pattern of defective administration and poor stewardship. He points to two other controversial city projects: Fisherman's Wharf, where state records show the city promised land it didn't own, and King's Landing, where a developer claims the city promised buildable property that contained 1,500 tons of old power plant concrete. Broderick said the city is planning to hire a real estate manager to oversee development decisions to prevent future situations.

cards.headline: Martin County School District to eliminate 58 positions, save nearly $4 million in reorganization
cards.body:
The Martin County School District plans to cut district staff as part of a reorganization for the upcoming school year, saving nearly $4 million from next year's budget. Superintendent Michael Maine told WPTV the plan includes eliminating 16 administrative and district-level positions, which includes three assistant principal positions, and removing 42 unfilled instructional vacancies. Maine said 10 of those vacancies were held in reserve, contingent on increasing enrollment. The changes are expected to save about $3.9 million from the district's projected budget next school year.

Maine said the reorganization eliminates positions he felt are no longer needed at the district office, with the district bearing a majority of the reduction. The cuts reflect how the district routinely manages staffing each year, according to Maine. He said the district looks at the number of students projected and allocates based on enrollment projections. Maine said for a district their size, the savings represent a lot of money. The Martin County School District currently enrolls 16,000 students.

Maine said the goal is to protect classroom resources while streamlining operations at the district level. He said the district can streamline and become more efficient at the district office with taxpayer dollars to be able to do more with less at the district versus at individual school sites. Maine described his approach to the reorganization simply, saying lean and mean is what he likes to say.

Not everyone is fully on board with the scope of the cuts. Abigal, whose son will be a fourth grader at Jensen Beach Elementary this fall, said she values the small class sizes and close teacher relationships the district currently offers. She said the teachers have one-to-one interactions with the kids and do a lot of different kinds of learning as well. Abigal said she hopes the district is careful about how deep the cuts go. She said the children need the admin, they need the teachers, and they need all the resources, as much as they can get.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Homeowner Faces Losing Home as Insurance Costs Hit $9,000 per Year
cards.body:
A Vero Beach homeowner says skyrocketing insurance costs may soon force her out of her home. Kelly Hagen says her homeowners insurance is $9,000 a year, which equates to $750 a month on top of her mortgage payment. Her home has three bedrooms and two baths, is about 1,500 square feet and was built in 1994. Hagen says the financial pressure from the premium increases has become unbearable, and she reached out to share her frustration over the relentless rise in costs.

Hagen says her insurance went from $6,000 to $8,000 the next year and keeps going up. Her insurance company requires impact windows, an expensive upgrade she has struggled to afford while working two jobs. Hagen works a full-time job and then works Instacart nights and weekends to try to make ends meet. She was turned away for a $10,000 My Safe Florida Home grant after it took too long to find a contractor, a roadblock many Florida homeowners have faced. The situation has left her with few options as costs continue to climb.

State leaders say now is the time for homeowners to shop around, pointing to new insurers entering the market with competitive rates. One new company, Stand Insurance, is offering to help homeowners connect with affordable contractors. Stand uses AI technology to study homes and then works to pair homeowners with vendors and contractors to make repairs. "If you can actually help someone be safer and have their home be safer, it's beneficial to everyone involved; we don't have to pay out in claims and customers pay less in premiums," Dan Preston, the CEO of Stand Insurance, said.

Hagen said she can probably hang on just a couple more months with the increases in insurance. She said she will have to try and sell her house and that leaving would be devastating. The window to find a solution is closing fast for her as the mounting costs threaten to push her out of the home she has worked so hard to keep. Experts advise homeowners in similar situations to explore workable changes to their policy and shop around for lower premiums with other insurance companies.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: The 44-year-old tennis star pulled out of her doubles match after draining fluid from her right knee following a three-set singles loss earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted on Instagram that she was heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles and that coming back to compete again has been a gift. She said the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to her, but her knee is not ready to compete. The post included images of four syringes showing the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday.

The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that was not scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Venus, 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again soon, saying to stay tuned to a city near you.

cards.headline: Argentina survives 3-2 thriller against Cape Verde to advance in World Cup
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his 20th career World Cup goal as Argentina narrowly defeated Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time in South Florida.
cards.body:
Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a World Cup Round of 32 match that went to extra time, with the defending champion surviving a scare from the tiny island nation. The go-ahead score was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina advanced to face Egypt, which beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday, in Atlanta on Tuesday. Messi now has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: FIFA lifts Folarin Balogun suspension after Trump calls FIFA president
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump intervened on behalf of the American striker, whose red-card suspension was lifted ahead of Monday's World Cup match against Belgium.
cards.body:
The FIFA Disciplinary Committee confirmed that United States striker Folarin Balogun will be eligible to play against Belgium on Monday in Seattle after his one-match suspension was lifted. The 25-year-old forward was facing an automatic suspension following a straight red card during the United States 2-0 Round of 32 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina on July 1. Balogun was sent off in the 64th minute following a VAR review for a challenge that stepped on the ankle of Bosnian defender Tarik Muharemovic, an offense classified under serious foul play. FIFA elected to utilize Article 27 of its code, which allows the judicial body to fully or partially suspend the implementation of an on-pitch disciplinary measure under a probationary period. The committee noted that the implementation of the match suspension is suspended for a probationary period of one year.

U.S. Soccer expressed satisfaction with the outcome and said the team's full attention is focused on the Round of 16 match against Belgium in Seattle. Balogun has been the focal point of coach Mauricio Pochettino's high-pressing attack and is the team's top scorer of the tournament with three goals in four matches. President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to applaud FIFA's decision, posting "Thank you to FIFA for doing what was right, and reversing a great injustice! TRUMP." FIFA previously used Article 27 in November to clear Portuguese captain Cristiano Ronaldo, who faced a three-match ban for violent conduct after receiving a straight red card for an elbow against the Republic of Ireland during a qualifier.

cards.headline: Belgium federation outraged after FIFA lifts Balogun suspension following Trump call
cards.teaser: The Royal Belgian Football Association said it is investigating options after FIFA lifted the American striker's suspension in what appears to be the first time since 1962 a World Cup red card did not result in a suspension.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino after the United States game against Bosnia and Herzegovina asking FIFA to review the red card given to Folarin Balogun, according to a person familiar with the call who spoke on condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to speak publicly about the matter. Balogun received a red card for stepping awkwardly on the right ankle of Tarik Muharemović of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 2-0 round of 32 win on Wednesday, triggering an automatic one-game suspension. FIFA announced Sunday that the suspension had been lifted for the round of 16 match against Belgium on Monday, an extraordinary move that triggered praise from Trump and outrage from Belgium's team. It appeared to be the first time since 1962 that a red card during a World Cup did not result in a suspension. Trump said in a statement on social media thanking FIFA for doing what was right and reversing a great injustice.

The Royal Belgian Football Association said it was astonished by the decision. Belgium coach Rudi Garcia said through a translator that he didn't know that in the offices of FIFA the fifth of July was the first of April in Europe. Garcia said the Belgian federation defends football in general, its integrity and ethics, calling it the first time in World Cup history for this kind of decision. The RBFA said it is investigating all potential options to safeguard the legitimate rights of all participating teams and protect the fundamental principles of fair play. Brazilian referee Raphael Claus didn't initially signal a card but showed Balogun red after a video review. U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino said the team was punished enough against Bosnia and Herzegovina to play with 10 men for 30 minutes in a decision that was completely unfair.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state championship after 10-2 season and district title
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year seniors, with the majority coming from the middle school program. Robertson said the players know how things are run and have had success in their careers, and he hopes their senior year will be the best season the program has had.

The Scots are taking on a more challenging schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams said the team wants to take the program to the next level by playing against really good teams and attracting new people. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs, noting the team wants to go undefeated in the regular season but that does not matter if they keep losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to, allowing the team to work harder so they can see positive results when they come off the season and break their record.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Scheduled for Vero Beach in November
hero.teaser: Under The Sun Promotions announced the return of the Treasure Coast Seafood Festival to Vero Beach this November.
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival is returning to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The annual event brings seafood vendors and entertainment to the Treasure Coast each year.

Under The Sun Promotions announced the festival's return on Monday. Additional details about the November event dates and location have not yet been released.

hero.headline: DeSantis closes final bill-signing season after reshaping Florida law across eight years
hero.body:
Ron DeSantis has likely wrapped his final regular bill-signing season, closing one of his last major opportunities to shape Florida law from the governor's desk. With the new fiscal year underway and DeSantis term-limited from seeking another consecutive term, the regular lawmaking window for his administration is essentially closed barring a future special session, emergency response or other extraordinary action. Florida's Constitution bars a governor who has served more than six years across two consecutive terms from being elected to the succeeding term.

A review of regular-session action shows the scale of DeSantis' eight years in office: 2,037 regular-session bills signed since 2019, along with 66 regular-session vetoes. His busiest year came in 2023, when 341 regular-session bills became law. His lightest was his first year, 2019, with 189. The laws reshaped major parts of Florida's life. Under DeSantis, Florida expanded school choice, with the governor signing HB 1 in 2023 to eliminate income restrictions and open scholarship programs more broadly to students across the state. He also signed new abortion restrictions, including Florida's six-week ban, after first approving a 15-week restriction earlier in his tenure. Additional legislation included permitless carry, expanded immigration enforcement, COVID-era limits on vaccine and mask mandates, new election laws, restrictions on diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and major property insurance changes. DeSantis also signed 2026 legislation giving Florida new authority tied to terrorist organization designations and additional limits on local DEI programs, continuing a broader conservative policy push in his final years in office. That agenda became central to the national brand DeSantis promoted as the Florida blueprint, a fast-moving conservative policy model powered by Republican control of the Legislature and the governor's office.

DeSantis also used his veto power to block dozens of bills. In 2022, he vetoed a net-metering bill that critics said would have hurt rooftop solar customer incentives. That same year, DeSantis vetoed an alimony overhaul, citing concerns about retroactivity. In 2024, he vetoed hemp restrictions, arguing the bill would impose heavy regulatory burdens on small businesses. In 2026, he vetoed a sovereign immunity bill that would have increased lawsuit limits against state and local government entities.

Over eight years, DeSantis vetoed roughly $10.6 billion in spending, using Florida's line-item veto power to cut local projects, trim legislative priorities and reinforce his image as a fiscal conservative. In June, DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year after nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, with his office calling it the fourth straight year of declining state spending. Democrats and local officials have often criticized those cuts, arguing they hit community projects, infrastructure needs and social services. After more than 2,000 regular-session bills signed, 66 regular-session vetoes and billions cut from state spending, DeSantis leaves behind a Florida lawbook that looks far different than the one he inherited in 2019.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds dominates Florida GOP governor debate he refused to attend
cards.teaser: The Trump-backed frontrunner was mentioned at least 60 times by rivals Paul Renner, Jay Collins and James Fishback, who criticized his refusal to appear on stage.
cards.body:
Florida's first major Republican debate for governor was dominated by the candidate who skipped it. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins and businessman James Fishback took the stage Thursday night, each trying to prove he is the strongest alternative to U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-backed frontrunner. Donalds was mentioned by name at least 60 times throughout the two-hour event. Moderator Patrick Bet-David opened by calling Donalds "the elephant not in the room." He said he had urged Donalds to attend, but Donalds' position was that he has raised roughly $100 million, polling between 48% to 58%, and would only consider debating once another candidate hits double digits. Collins hit Donalds for refusing to debate, saying, "We don't do kings in the United States of America. We sure don't do them in Florida." Renner called Donalds' absence disrespectful and argued Donalds is avoiding the stage because he cannot prove he is better qualified. Fishback contrasted Donalds' fundraising with his own ground game, saying his campaign made history by being the first campaign in Florida running for governor to visit all 67 counties.

The debate itself centered on affordability, property taxes, insurance and hyperscale data centers. Fishback promised to completely and totally abolish property taxes in the state of Florida and pledged to take a "chainsaw" to local government spending. Collins said cities and counties have a spending problem and need more accountability. Renner said the current property-tax amendment does not go far enough, pitching his own Florida First plan to eliminate most homestead property taxes while shifting more burden to tourists, out-of-state investors and large corporations. The sharpest clash came over data centers, with Fishback promising to reject and remove every experimental data center in Florida while Renner said he would call a special session to stop hyperscale projects. Collins urged local control with state guardrails, prompting Fishback to mock his answer as a "word salad."

hero.headline: Martin County School District to eliminate 58 positions, save nearly $4 million in reorganization
hero.body:
The Martin County School District plans to cut district staff as part of a reorganization for the upcoming school year, saving nearly $4 million from next year's budget. Superintendent Michael Maine told WPTV the plan includes eliminating 16 administrative and district-level positions, which includes three assistant principal positions, and removing 42 unfilled instructional vacancies. Maine said 10 of those vacancies were held in reserve, contingent on increasing enrollment. The changes are expected to save about $3.9 million from the district's projected budget next school year.

Maine said the reorganization eliminates positions he felt are no longer needed at the district office, with the district bearing a majority of the reduction. The cuts reflect how the district routinely manages staffing each year, according to Maine. He said the district looks at the number of students projected and allocates based on enrollment projections. Maine said for a district their size, the savings represent a lot of money. The Martin County School District currently enrolls 16,000 students.

Maine said the goal is to protect classroom resources while streamlining operations at the district level. He said the district can streamline and become more efficient at the district office with taxpayer dollars to be able to do more with less at the district versus at individual school sites. Maine described his approach to the reorganization simply, saying lean and mean is what he likes to say.

Not everyone is fully on board with the scope of the cuts. Abigal, whose son will be a fourth grader at Jensen Beach Elementary this fall, said she values the small class sizes and close teacher relationships the district currently offers. She said the teachers have one-to-one interactions with the kids and do a lot of different kinds of learning as well. Abigal said she hopes the district is careful about how deep the cuts go. She said the children need the admin, they need the teachers, and they need all the resources, as much as they can get.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound gets first Aldi grocery store July 9 at former Winn-Dixie site
cards.teaser: Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi store on July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road, in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be.
cards.body: The new grocery store is opening July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road, in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be. Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years. There will be a grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 9 at 8:30 a.m., and the first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card. The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m.

hero.headline: Construction begins on 18-hole golf course at Esplanade at Solaeris in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
Taylor Morrison has started construction on an 18-hole golf course at Esplanade at Solaeris, the company's new golf residential community in Port St. Lucie. The course is designed by Wilczynski.

The Esplanade at Solaeris development represents Taylor Morrison's entry into the golf community market in Port St. Lucie. The community will combine residential housing with golf amenities.

The Wilczynski-designed course will serve as the centerpiece of the residential development. Taylor Morrison is building the community to attract golfers and families seeking access to golf facilities.

The construction marks the first phase of the golf course development at the Port St. Lucie site. Taylor Morrison has not announced a completion date for the course.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Homeowner Faces Losing Home as Insurance Costs Hit $9,000 per Year
hero.body:
A Vero Beach homeowner says skyrocketing insurance costs may soon force her out of her home. Kelly Hagen says her homeowners insurance is $9,000 a year, which equates to $750 a month on top of her mortgage payment. Her home has three bedrooms and two baths, is about 1,500 square feet and was built in 1994. Hagen says the financial pressure from the premium increases has become unbearable, and she reached out to share her frustration over the relentless rise in costs.

Hagen says her insurance went from $6,000 to $8,000 the next year and keeps going up. Her insurance company requires impact windows, an expensive upgrade she has struggled to afford while working two jobs. Hagen works a full-time job and then works Instacart nights and weekends to try to make ends meet. She was turned away for a $10,000 My Safe Florida Home grant after it took too long to find a contractor, a roadblock many Florida homeowners have faced. The situation has left her with few options as costs continue to climb.

State leaders say now is the time for homeowners to shop around, pointing to new insurers entering the market with competitive rates. One new company, Stand Insurance, is offering to help homeowners connect with affordable contractors. Stand uses AI technology to study homes and then works to pair homeowners with vendors and contractors to make repairs. "If you can actually help someone be safer and have their home be safer, it's beneficial to everyone involved; we don't have to pay out in claims and customers pay less in premiums," Dan Preston, the CEO of Stand Insurance, said.

Hagen said she can probably hang on just a couple more months with the increases in insurance. She said she will have to try and sell her house and that leaving would be devastating. The window to find a solution is closing fast for her as the mounting costs threaten to push her out of the home she has worked so hard to keep. Experts advise homeowners in similar situations to explore workable changes to their policy and shop around for lower premiums with other insurance companies.
